subject: Clarifying indemnity for model outputs / onboarding checklist
messages:
From: Asha Srinivasan <asha@marketlytics.com>
To: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
Cc: legal@marketlytics.com
Date: 2026-08-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify indemnity for model outputs — onboarding

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick start on onboarding. Our procurement counsel has flagged the indemnity language in the draft MSA / Order Form related to third-party claims for output generated by models. Specifically, MarketLytics needs clarity on two items before we can finalize the Order Form: 

1) Scope: Are you able to defend and indemnify for third-party IP claims that arise from model outputs (e.g., an output that allegedly infringes a third party's patent or copyright)? 
2) Evidence / defense mechanics: What evidence will Redwood provide (training data provenance, SOC2 artifacts, evidence custody) and what is the expected notice/assistance cadence if a claim arises? 

We appreciate that vendors are cautious about open-model outputs; our product team is relying on generated content in a customer-facing feature and we need a clear mechanism for risk transfer or mitigation.

Can you share your typical customer compromise (custody of defense, notice window, cap approach) and an onboarding checklist for evidence that procurement can use? We have a hard procurement window of two weeks to sign to meet our launch. Looping in Maya from our outside counsel (cc).

Thanks,
Asha Srinivasan
Head of Procurement, MarketLytics
asha@marketlytics.com

--
MarketLytics Legal <legal@marketlytics.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Clarify indemnity for model outputs — onboarding

Chloe / team,

Draft position below — aiming for a balance between MarketLytics' procurement needs and our risk appetite. Short version up top, proposed clause language below. We'll include this as an Order Form addendum.

High-level compromise (recommended):
- Redwood will "defend and indemnify" for third-party claims alleging that Redwood's model outputs infringe a third party's IP, but only where (i) the output was generated by a Redwood-hosted model (not a model customer self-hosts); (ii) the alleged infringing content was not provided or instructed by the customer (customer prompts or uploaded content are excluded); and (iii) the customer provides prompt notice and reasonable cooperation.
- Cap: aggregate liability for these claims limited to the fees paid under the Order Form in the 12 months preceding notice (standard market approach for higher-risk outputs). Alternative: a fixed cap equal to 3x annual fees if they push back.
- Defense control: Redwood to have primary defense control, but we must allow MarketLytics to participate with counsel at their own cost. If Redwood elects to settle, settlement can't include admission of liability binding the customer without their consent.
- Evidence: we will provide a packaged evidence bundle (SOC2 Type II report, model training-data provenance summary, runtime trace logs for the disputed request, and a redacted sample of training sources where applicable). Some elements may be limited by third-party dataset licensing — we should call that out in the addendum.

Proposed short clause (for Order Form addendum):
"Vendor will defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer from third-party claims alleging that Content generated solely by Vendor-operated models infringes the third party's intellectual property, provided that: (a) Customer gives Vendor prompt written notice of the claim; (b) Customer provides reasonable cooperation and authority to control the defense; (c) the claim does not arise from Customer-supplied content, prompts, or instructions; and (d) Vendor's aggregate liability for such claims shall not exceed the fees paid by Customer under this Order Form during the 12 months preceding the claim. Vendor may settle on commercially reasonable terms but may not enter into any settlement that admits Customer liability without Customer's prior written consent."

Attachments: internal_redline.docx (contains alternative cap language and fallback reimburse-only path).

Neha, can you draft the one-page evidence checklist we can attach? Dylan, what's a realistic handover SLA? I suggested initial triage within 48 hours and full evidence package within 5 business days depending on scope (may need legal hold).

-K

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: chloe_martin@redwood.ai
To: Asha Srinivasan <asha@marketlytics.com>, MarketLytics Legal <legal@marketlytics.com>, Maya Patel <maya@vendorcounsel.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, neha_kapoor@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-30T08:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify indemnity for model outputs — onboarding (proposed addendum + checklist)

Hi Asha / Maya,

Thanks — below is the short proposal we discussed internally and the onboarding evidence checklist. Attaching OrderForm_v3.docx (with addendum inserted) and ML_Data_Evidence_List.pdf (one-page checklist). We want to keep your launch timing intact; if this looks acceptable we'll request a redline-only review.

Summary (proposal):
- Scope: Redwood will defend & indemnify for third-party IP claims tied to content generated solely by Redwood-hosted models. Customer-provided inputs (prompts, uploads) are excluded.
- Cap: fees paid under the Order Form in the prior 12 months (we can discuss 3x alternative if your counsel prefers).
- Defense: Redwood retains defense control, Customer may participate with counsel at its cost. Redwood will not enter a settlement that binds Customer to an admission of liability without Customer consent.
- Evidence & timing: On notice, Customer will provide initial claim notice and any contextual materials. Redwood will: (a) acknowledge receipt within 24 business hours, (b) perform an initial triage within 48 hours, and (c) deliver the packaged evidence (SOC2 Type II, training-data provenance summary, runtime request logs) within 5 business days where available. Some provenance detail may be redacted or limited by third-party licensing — we flag that in the addendum.

Short onboarding checklist (attached):
- SOC2 Type II report (redacted acceptable)
- Model provenance summary and version (model id, date, quantization/variant)
- Runtime request logs for the disputed request (timestamps, request id)
- Known third-party licensed data limitations statement
- Point of contact for legal/ops handover (we’ve suggested Redwood security@redwood.ai)

If this high-level compromise works for MarketLytics, can we get a redline back by EOD Friday (2026-09-03) or a scheduled 30-minute call this week to finalize? We have attached a DocuSign-ready OrderForm link if you want to proceed after redline.

Attachments: OrderForm_v3.docx, ML_Data_Evidence_List.pdf

Best,
Chloe Martin
Product Partnerships
Redwood Inference
